name: @peapod/api
description: Peapod's Node/Fastify API. Owns the domain database, the row-level policy table, the realtime hub, the scheduled jobs, and the reward ledger. Holds no credentials (services/security owns those) and performs no heavy maths (services/compute owns that, with a TypeScript fallback from @peapod/shared).
//--- module system ---: ESM everywhere, matching @peapod/shared. Relative imports therefore carry an explicit .js extension even in .ts source, because Node resolves the emitted specifier verbatim.

scripts.//--- development ---: tsx watches and transpiles on the fly; no build step while iterating.
scripts.//--- production ---: tsc emits plain ESM into dist/; start runs it with no transpiler in the loop.
scripts.build: tsc -p tsconfig.json && node --input-type=module -e "import { copyFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'; mkdirSync('dist/db',{recursive:true}); copyFileSync('src/db/bootstrap.sql','dist/db/bootstrap.sql');"
scripts.//--- quality gates ---: Run both before finishing any change. typecheck needs @peapod/shared built first (npm run build:shared at the repo root).
scripts.//--- database ---: generate diffs src/db/schema.ts against drizzle/ and writes a new SQL migration; migrate applies pending ones; seed loads the demo pod.

//--- why there is no HTTP client depend: Node 20 ships a spec-compliant global fetch and AbortSignal.timeout(). Both outbound clients (services/security, services/compute) use them, so undici is not installed: one less dependency to keep patched, and identical behaviour.
//--- why there is no AWS SDK ---: src/services/storage.ts signs S3 PUT URLs with AWS Signature Version 4 using node:crypto only. Presigning is ~60 lines of HMAC; the SDK would add tens of megabytes to the image for that one function.
